clue.text: One is not sure about taking these steps

definitions.text: One is not sure about taking these steps

parts.words: One is not sure about taking these steps
parts.note: someone unsure about a move hesitates, and the steps are those of a ballroom dance named after that pause

explanation.surface: A nervous person dithers over whether to take a course of action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' looks like a figure of speech for actions, but it is literal dance steps; the hesitation waltz is an old ballroom dance with pauses built into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballroom dance in three-four time featuring deliberate pauses, so its dancer seems to falter mid-step.

clue.text: Skill needed to get centaur on board?

parts.note: a centaur of Greek myth is half horse, half man, so literally a horse-man
to be on board is to be aboard a ship

explanation.surface: Asks what ability is needed to get a mythical beast onto a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful literal reading of centaur as a horse plus a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The ability to ride and manage a mount well is a recognised accomplishment.

clue.text: It's separate this decision

definitions.meaning: a boxing verdict where the judges disagree is a decision of this kind

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a particular ruling divides opinion.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide is a synonym for parting, and a verdict on which the judges disagree is called by this word.

clue.text: Made correct mark at the start having been reprimanded

parts.note: putting a check mark against a right answer
off means at the start, as when a race is off

explanation.surface: A teacher marked work right at first, then got told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off' is used for the start of a race or journey: 'they're off'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being told off sharply is the same as being scolded or rebuked.

clue.text: Be unwell with nurse round at last

indicators.note: round says the nursing word goes around the illness word

parts.note: to nurse is to tend
to ail is to be unwell

explanation.surface: A patient finally feels ill with a nurse in attendance.
explanation.definitionFit: The final portion or very end of something, so reaching it means arriving finally.

clue.text: Oops! Breaks down total, it's beastly

indicators.note: the letters of the exclamation are broken down and reassembled

parts.note: a sum is a total

explanation.surface: An exclamation as someone's addition goes wrong in an awful way.
explanation.definitionFit: A marsupial animal of the Americas, so a creature or beast.

clue.text: Old eccentric from western Australia first had mechanical gadget

indicators.note: first had says the western and Australia letters come before the rest

parts.note: A is the international abbreviation for Australia

indicators.note: eccentric means odd, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: An odd old person from the west of Australia once owned a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' looks like an adjective for the eccentric, but it is the anagram fodder; 'first had' puts the abbreviation for Western Australia in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote manipulator device that lets an operator handle things at a distance by machinery.

clue.text: The Andes, for instance, is such a target

definitions.text: The Andes, for instance, is such a target

parts.words: The Andes, for instance, is such a target
parts.note: a mountain chain stretching a great distance, and a target far away from the shooter

explanation.surface: A distant mountain chain is described as something to aim at.
explanation.definitionFit: A great mountain chain stretches a vast distance, and a distant shot needs weapons with much reach.

clue.text: Widow does not have time for thing of the past

indicators.note: does not have says one letter is removed from the widow word

parts.note: relict is an old word for a widow

explanation.surface: A widow is too busy for something old-fashioned.
explanation.walkthrough: RELICT, an archaic word for a widow, loses its T.
explanation.definitionFit: An object surviving from an earlier era, a remnant of history.

clue.text: Removed silicone from area of rock strata

indicators.note: removed suggests the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone took sealant away from a geological site.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed' reads as taking away, but means moved again: the letters of SILICONE are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A geological line or zone where strata dip at the same angle.

clue.text: In places making up both ends of the journey

definitions.text: In places making up both ends of the journey

parts.words: In places making up both ends of the journey
parts.note: a trip runs from one spot to another, so its starting and finishing points describe scattered locations

explanation.surface: Something found at the start and the finish of a trip.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means dotted about in various spots, and a journey goes from this spot to that one.

clue.text: Radical point

explanation.definitionFit: A drastic view is far out, and the outermost tip of anything is its furthest point.

clue.text: Whip gently starts entering new course

indicators.note: entering says the first letter goes inside the scrambled word
new tells us to make a fresh arrangement of the letters
starts picks the opening letter of gently

explanation.surface: A jockey's whip is gently brought in on a new racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges COURSE into SCOURE, and 'entering' puts G (from 'gently starts') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lash used for flogging, a synonym for a whip.

clue.text: On which one has no obligation to buy

definitions.text: On which one has no obligation to buy

parts.words: On which one has no obligation to buy
parts.note: goods taken home on trial terms may be returned without purchase

explanation.surface: Describes a shopping arrangement with no commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: The British short form for 'approval', as in goods sent 'on approval' to be returned if unwanted.
explanation.definitionFit: A colloquial short form for trial terms of sale, when goods may be sent back without paying.

clue.text: Penny and I went round town hesitantly for radioactive element

indicators.note: went round says penny and I surround the town

parts.note: Luton is a town in Bedfordshire, England
um is the sound a hesitant speaker makes

explanation.surface: Two people nervously wandered around a town looking for a dangerous metal.
explanation.walkthrough: Luton is a town in Bedfordshire, north of London; 'went round' means the penny and the I enclose it, and the hesitation sound follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy man-made metallic element, number 94, used in nuclear weapons and reactors.

clue.text: Exchange income and gain ascendancy

indicators.note: exchange says the letters are swapped around into a new order

explanation.surface: Trading earnings to get the upper hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exchange' rearranges INCOME and AND; 'gain' joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Supremacy or control over others, the state of having the upper hand.

clue.text: Dandy serf not in us city

parts.note: Beau Nash was a famous Georgian dandy in Bath

indicators.note: not says the word in is taken out of the serf word

parts.note: a villein was a feudal serf

explanation.surface: A fashionable man who is not a peasant lives in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: VILLEIN, a medieval serf, loses IN to give VILLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Tennessee, known for country music, is an American city.

clue.text: Evasively preparing to offer new deal

definitions.meaning: acting in a shifty, evasive manner
mixing playing cards before dealing them again

explanation.definitionFit: Shifty behaviour is evasive, and a card player mixes the pack before a fresh hand is dealt.

clue.text: But this craft is not used for winter cruises

definitions.text: But this craft is not used for winter cruises

parts.words: But this craft is not used for winter cruises
parts.note: a vessel sailing over frozen water is used in winter, but on runners, not for pleasure voyages at sea

explanation.surface: A boat that, oddly, isn't for holiday trips in the cold season.
explanation.definitionFit: A sailing vessel on runners that skims over frozen lakes, a winter craft.

clue.text: Some vulgar mention of item of clothing

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone makes a coarse reference to a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft's definition included 'of', which is a link word; the definition is 'item of clothing'.
explanation.definitionFit: Any article of dress worn on the body.

clue.text: Good fellow, one in Germany, a mug!

parts.note: a saint, abbreviated ST, is a good person
ein is German for one

explanation.surface: A German man is called a nice chap but a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like a gullible person, but is a beer tankard.
explanation.definitionFit: A large earthenware beer tankard, a drinking vessel.

clue.text: Mineral Ronald takes round in anger

indicators.note: in says the name and the circle go inside the anger word

parts.note: ire is anger
Ron is short for Ronald
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A man called Ronald angrily takes a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock from which a metal is extracted, a natural mineral deposit.

clue.text: Mainly it contains water

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the sea, which mostly consists of water

explanation.surface: A statement that something is largely water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' looks like 'mostly', but hints at 'the main', a poetic term for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast body of salt water, the open sea.

clue.text: Recall

parts.note: read as re-call, to call on again, a second visit

explanation.definitionFit: To call again on a place or person is to go back to see it.

clue.text: Fixed to fight

parts.note: fixed means set firmly

explanation.surface: Someone is determined to have a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief quarrel or scrap, a squabble.

clue.text: Enemy area! One of 24 around earth

parts.note: time is the enemy, as in the saying
a zone is an area

explanation.surface: A hostile region of the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time is the enemy' is a common expression; there are 24 hourly divisions of the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe is divided into 24 longitudinal bands, each keeping its own standard hour.

clue.text: Fired about a quantity of liquid

parts.note: a fire that is lit has been set going
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone sacked over a measure of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of volume, a measure for fluids.

clue.text: Approaching enemy without king gaining prominence

parts.note: coming to means approaching, as in coming to a place

indicators.note: without means outside, so the enemy phrase goes around the king

parts.note: the foe is the enemy
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: An enemy draws near minus its king and grows notorious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means 'outside': THE FOE goes round R, the Latin rex.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming conspicuous, moving into the forefront of attention.
